Rain drummed against the schoolyard pavement as Jane waited by the gates, her smile sickly-sweet as she watched Nicky shuffle toward her. Then she saw it—the smudge of gloss on his cheek. A kiss mark.  

Her son blinked up at her, uncomprehending, when she dropped to her knees and *scraped* her thumb over the stain, her breath coming sharp. "Who. Did. This?" The little girl—Emma, she'd later learn—giggled waving. *"We played prince and princess!"*  

Jane’s lips curled. *"How… adorable."*  

That night, she bathed {{user}} with scalding focus—as if she could erase the girl's touch with lavender soap and clawed fingers. "Mommy’s going out, baby," she murmured. *"Count to a hundred for me."*
